template.name: The Vernon Inheritance: A House Divided

assignments.text:
And what in human form could have given a
more complete impersonation of the morning than
this girl, fresh, fair, and strong, with such a world of
latent possibilities in her? The cloud of last night's
perversity blew away. She met the eye of the day
with a gaze as open and as confident. Neither
Nature nor Hester had any fear.
assignments.summary: Hester becomes one with the radiant morning; her troubles dissolve and she embodies fearless youth and boundless potential.
assignments.best_quote: And what in human form could have given a more complete impersonation of the morning than this girl, fresh, fair, and strong, with such a world of latent possibilities in her? The cloud of last night's perversity blew away. She met the eye of the day with a gaze as open and as confident. Neither Nature nor Hester had any fear.

assignments.text:
It was only thus,
except by concerted meetings which would have
solved the question, that they could meet at all, and
the grotesque incongruity of such surroundings with
the matter in the foreground, sometimes affected
Hester with a sort of moral sickness and disgust. The scene seemed to throw a certain unworthiness,
levity, unelevated aspect upon the question altogether—as
if this thing which was to affect two lives was
no more than an engagement for a dance.
assignments.summary: The frivolous ballroom setting makes the most important question of their lives seem trivial and unworthy, producing in Hester a sense of moral sickness.
assignments.best_quote: The scene seemed to throw a certain unworthiness, levity, unelevated aspect upon the question altogether—as if this thing which was to affect two lives was no more than an engagement for a dance.

assignments.text:
On the other, Edward, in all a bridegroom's
excitement, with the woman he loved beside
him, travelling far away into the night, flushed with
pleasure, with novelty, with the success of his actions
whatever they were, and with the world before him. It seemed to Hester that she saw the two scenes,
although she herself would have to be an actor in
one of them if it ever came to pass. She saw them
to the most insignificant details.
assignments.summary: Hester imagines the bank in ruin with desperate customers and Harry helpless, while Edward and his lover escape into the night.
assignments.best_quote: She saw them to the most insignificant details.

assignments.text:
In the midst of this
pale and colourless illumination Hester's white face,
with the blue veins showing in it, in an attitude of
utter abandonment and exhaustion, pillowed upon
the dark cushions of the chair, was the central point;
her hand with the pen in it was still on the table, the
candles flickering with a yellow uncertain blaze. Catherine went and stood by her for a moment and
looked at her.
assignments.summary: In the strange light, Hester's pale, exhausted face with visible blue veins becomes the focal point, her hand still holding the pen, surrounded by flickering candles.
assignments.best_quote: In the midst of this pale and colourless illumination Hester's white face, with the blue veins showing in it, in an attitude of utter abandonment and exhaustion, pillowed upon the dark cushions of the chair, was the central point

assignments.text:
"Which there is not, thank God," she said heartily. And again there ensued that little pause. Was it
possible she did not observe it? No one echoed the
sentiment, no one even murmured the little nothings
with which a stillness, which has a meaning, is
generally filled up by some benevolent bystander. What did it mean? Hester asked herself. But
Catherine took no notice. All had gone so well with
her. She was not afraid of evil tidings.
assignments.summary: Catherine warmly asserts that work is not needed, but another charged silence falls; no one corroborates her sentiment, and the narrator reveals her dangerous lack of fear or suspicion.
assignments.best_quote: All had gone so well with her. She was not afraid of evil tidings.

assignments.text:
"I beg your pardon, Miss Hester," he cried, "I
was just going to tell something of your mother that
would please you. When I told her we wanted
money, she ran to her desk and got out all she had. It was twenty pounds," said the old clerk with a [Pg 136] 
little laugh; "twenty pounds, when we wanted twice
as many thousands! But what did that matter?
assignments.summary: Mr. Rule tells Hester that when asked for help, her mother gave her entire savings of twenty pounds, though thousands were needed—an act of selfless devotion.
assignments.best_quote: When I told her we wanted money, she ran to her desk and got out all she had. It was twenty pounds.

assignments.text:
Hester's heart gave a bound of mingled pleasure
and pain. Perhaps even she had never done justice
to her simple-hearted mother. She sat bolt upright
in her chair, listening with all her might. Catherine
Vernon seemed to retire from the principal place she
had hitherto held in the conversation, and Hester
came forward in her stead. She looked at the old
clerk steadily.
assignments.summary: Hester, moved by the revelation of her mother's sacrifice, sits upright with keen attention; Catherine withdraws from the center of conversation as Hester steps forward.
assignments.best_quote: Hester's heart gave a bound of mingled pleasure and pain.

assignments.text:
"You speak," she said, "of ladies only. Where
was my father?" holding Rule with her eye, so that
he could not escape.
assignments.summary: Hester demands to know where her father was during the crisis when her mother and cousin helped save the bank.
assignments.best_quote: You speak of ladies only. Where was my father?

assignments.text:
"I don't wish to look again. Is not that enough? I suppose it would make her very unhappy. She
would struggle, she would try to find excuses. Oh,
Captain Morgan, don't press me so! I suppose everything
would turn round and round. There would
seem nothing to stand on, nothing to look up to,
the skies would all whirl and the solid ground.
assignments.summary: Hester struggles to articulate the true emotional impact: everything becomes unstable and vertiginous; she is nearly overcome describing it.
assignments.best_quote: There would seem nothing to stand on, nothing to look up to, the skies would all whirl and the solid ground. It makes my head swim to think of it.

template.name: The Social Machinery of Victorian Life

assignments.text:
"Sir!" said Mrs. John Vernon, standing in a fine
attitude of displeasure by her desk, holding it open
with one hand. She looked like a picture by Sir
Thomas Lawrence, her scarf, for she wore a scarf,
hanging half off her pretty white shoulders, caught
upon one equally white arm, her ringlets waving on
her cheek. His laugh was rude, and then he was
only a clerk.
assignments.summary: Mrs. John Vernon stands in displeasure by her desk, her beauty and refinement momentarily masking her helplessness, like a Lawrence portrait of aristocratic offended dignity.
assignments.best_quote: Sir!

assignments.text:
Miss Vernon's was a reign of great benevolence,
of great liberality, but of great firmness too. As
she got older she became almost the most important
person in Redborough. The people spoke of her,
as they sometimes do of a very popular man, by
her Christian name. Catherine Vernon did this
and that, they said. Catherine Vernon was the first
thought when anything was wanted either by the
poor who needed help, or the philanthropist who
wanted to give it.
assignments.summary: Catherine becomes the most important person in Redborough, consulted for all matters of philanthropy and civic need; people refer to her by her Christian name.
assignments.best_quote: Catherine Vernon did this and that, they said. Catherine Vernon was the first thought when anything was wanted either by the poor who needed help, or the philanthropist who wanted to give it

assignments.text:
"My dear, I could do it—without difficulty. Is
it just, do you think, that one human creature
should be made the victim of another, simply because
he has been instrumental in bringing that other into
the world? Supposing that they have drained all
that was best in me out of me for years? Supposing
that they have made my life hard and bitter to me?
assignments.summary: Captain Morgan challenges the justice of parental obligation, asking whether a parent should be victimized by children they brought into the world.
assignments.best_quote: Is it just, do you think, that one human creature should be made the victim of another, simply because he has been instrumental in bringing that other into the world?

assignments.text:
He
reflected benevolently, with a contemptuous good
nature, that he could get back to the bank in time
still to liberate his cousin, so that everybody would
be satisfied. This he did, stopping at the telegraph
office on the way. His despatch was as follows:—"Proceed,
but with caution. Needful will be forthcoming."
He drew a long breath when he thus
decided his fate; then he returned with all the ease
and relief which naturally comes with a decision.
assignments.summary: Edward stops at the telegraph office and sends Ashton a message authorizing the speculation, breathing relief that his fate is now decided.
assignments.best_quote: Proceed, but with caution. Needful will be forthcoming.

assignments.text:
"Oh, Edward!" she cried, "you have me and my
sympathy—even if you were wrong you should have my
sympathy. But is it just, is it good, do you think,
that you should ask all that and tell me nothing? I
am a woman, but I am not a fool. I can understand
most things. Try me—tell me—I will set my mind
to it. Sympathy that is ignorant cannot be so good
as sympathy that knows."
assignments.summary: Hester declares she is not a fool and can understand most things; she demands to be tested and argues that informed sympathy is superior to ignorant loyalty.
assignments.best_quote: I am a woman, but I am not a fool. I can understand most things. Try me—tell me—I will set my mind to it. Sympathy that is ignorant cannot be so good as sympathy that knows.

template.name: Wit, Irony, and the Masks We Wear

assignments.text:
What an extraordinary shock
would it have been for his companion, who felt
herself to sit in the place of the audience, seeing
the puppets play their pranks upon the stage and
exhibit all their fooleries, to know that she herself
was the actor, turned outside in and seen through
in all her devices, to this boy whom she loved!
assignments.summary: The narrator delivers a brilliant ironic revelation: Catherine believes herself the audience observing the foolish actors of her little world, but is actually the actor being observed and judged by Edward, whom she loves.
assignments.best_quote: What an extraordinary shock would it have been for his companion, who felt herself to sit in the place of the audience, seeing the puppets play their pranks upon the stage and exhibit all their fooleries, to know that she herself was the actor, turned outside in and seen through in all her devices, to this boy whom she loved!

assignments.text:
Don't you think you would do better if you
warned her, or her mother?" Catherine's countenance
was so calm, her eyes so commanding, that
the Miss Vernon-Ridgways, altogether defeated in
their malicious intention, which was chiefly to wound
herself, felt their knees tremble under them, and
were genuinely awe-stricken for perhaps the first
time in their lives.
assignments.summary: Catherine's calm commanding tone and eyes terrify the Miss Vernon-Ridgways and make them feel they have failed to wound her.
assignments.best_quote: Don't you think you would do better if you warned her, or her mother?

assignments.text:
They had time and passion, and
universal human sympathy, on their side, whereas
the old people had none of all these, neither time to
wait, nor passion to inspire, nor sympathy anywhere
in heaven or earth. Catherine said to herself proudly
that she would not expose herself to the pity which
attends the vanquished. She would retire from the
fray.
assignments.summary: Understanding that age cannot compete with youth, Catherine resolves to withdraw with dignity rather than expose herself to sympathy.
assignments.best_quote: Catherine said to herself proudly that she would not expose herself to the pity which attends the vanquished. She would retire from the fray.

assignments.text:
When she reached the room in
which they had been at work, Hester, who had
answered as far as her faculties could to every call
upon her, had dropped back into the great chair in
which she had been sitting, and had fallen asleep in
utter exhaustion. It was a curious scene.
assignments.summary: Catherine returns to find Hester has fallen asleep in an armchair in utter exhaustion, creating a curious and poignant scene.

assignments.text:
It made him angry, it made
him furious; it made him for the moment too much
a natural man, too sincere and real to be capable of
his usual self-suppression. Harry would have an
equal share with himself of the bank; they were
equal there in power and authority, and in the
profits they drew. Why then was it that Harry
should be his own master and Edward the slave of
an old woman!
assignments.summary: Edward's anguish intensifies as he realizes that despite equal status and wealth in the bank, Harry possesses freedom while Edward remains enslaved to Catherine's emotional demands.
assignments.best_quote: Harry would have an equal share with himself of the bank; they were equal there in power and authority, and in the profits they drew. Why then was it that Harry should be his own master and Edward the slave of an old woman!

assignments.text:
He indemnified
himself by plunging into the midst of the
bundle of papers which he had not chosen to
describe to Catherine. In these papers lay far more
excitement than all Harry's privileges had yet
supplied. A battery of artillery planted in front of [Pg 219] 
this peaceful Grange with all its matches alight
would scarcely have been more full of danger.
assignments.summary: Edward finds psychological compensation for his powerlessness in dangerous financial papers that contain more excitement than Harry's romantic freedom.
assignments.best_quote: He indemnified himself by plunging into the midst of the bundle of papers which he had not chosen to describe to Catherine. In these papers lay far more excitement than all Harry's privileges had yet supplied. A battery of artillery planted in front of this peaceful Grange with all its matches alight would scarcely have been more full of danger.

assignments.text:
There was enough in the packet to tear the house
up by its roots, and send its walls flying in a whirlwind
of ashes and ruin. Edward sat down to
examine it as another man might have flown to
brandy or laudanum. Dreams were in it of sudden
successes, of fortunes achieved in a moment. Castles
in the air more dazzling than ever rose in a fairy
tale.
assignments.summary: The papers promise dazzling fantasies of sudden wealth and independence, to which Edward turns like a man seeking oblivion in drink or drugs.
assignments.best_quote: There was enough in the packet to tear the house up by its roots, and send its walls flying in a whirlwind of ashes and ruin. Edward sat down to examine it as another man might have flown to brandy or laudanum. Dreams were in it of sudden successes, of fortunes achieved in a moment. Castles in the air more dazzling than ever rose in a fairy tale.

assignments.text:
He revenged himself on his bonds, on the
superior happiness of his rival, on Catherine above
all, the unconscious cause of his imprisonment, by
this—Here was enough, all ready and in his hands,
to ruin them all.
assignments.summary: Edward projects his desire for revenge and liberation onto the papers, which offer the power to destroy Catherine and Harry simultaneously.
assignments.best_quote: He revenged himself on his bonds, on the superior happiness of his rival, on Catherine above all, the unconscious cause of his imprisonment, by this—Here was enough, all ready and in his hands, to ruin them all.

assignments.text:
"Oh, Hester, it would be easy, very easy, to cease to
be unfortunate—if you choose, dear. All that part
of our life might fly away like a cloud—if you
choose. We might be done with poverty and dependence
and thinking of what Catherine will say
and what people will think. The White House—might
be yours if you liked, everything might be
yours. You would only have to say the word."
assignments.summary: Mrs. John passionately describes the transformation marriage to Harry would bring: freedom from poverty, dependence, and Catherine's control, and the restoration of the White House.
assignments.best_quote: All that part of our life might fly away like a cloud—if you choose. We might be done with poverty and dependence and thinking of what Catherine will say and what people will think. The White House—might be yours if you liked, everything might be yours.

assignments.text:
She could put back her mother in
the White House she loved, take down the innocent
portrait in white satin, and hang it in the place of
honour once more; throw open finer rooms than
Catherine's for the reception of, oh! so different a
company—society in which no one should be overlooked,
and in which Catherine's gentle rival should
be supreme. She could do all this if she chose. The
thought suddenly bursting upon her made her head
go round.
assignments.summary: Hester envisions reversing her mother's exile from the White House and making herself a rival power centre to Catherine.
assignments.best_quote: She could put back her mother in the White House she loved, take down the innocent portrait in white satin, and hang it in the place of honour once more

assignments.text:
It gave her a sort of pang of amusement when she
concluded upon this—Hester! that proud, troublesome
creature—she who would never give in, who
put on the airs of a princess in the Grange drawing-room,
and declined to go to supper—she with the
spirit of a revolutionary, and the temper of a—demon—(no,
no, this was perhaps too bad—the
temper of a—Vernon, Catherine said to herself with
a laugh)—she to fall to the lot of Harry!
assignments.summary: Catherine finds the idea of Hester marrying Harry absurdly amusing—a paradoxical pairing of the ambitious, spirited girl with the placid, athletic young man.
assignments.best_quote: She to fall to the lot of Harry! This was so strangely funny, so paradoxical, so out of character, that it amused Catherine altogether beyond description, yet gave her a strange blow.

assignments.text:
Thus
she, who for the first moment had known no wish
but that of pushing homeward and hiding her
sudden downfall within her own house where
nobody could intrude upon her, had so triumphantly
explained all that trouble away before she got home,
that she entered the Grange radiant, with no sense
of having a downfall to hide. The casuistry of love
is more skilful than any device of philosophy. She
explained everything to herself.
assignments.summary: Catherine enters her home radiant, having completely explained away the scandal through the logic of love.
assignments.best_quote: The casuistry of love is more skilful than any device of philosophy. She explained everything to herself.

assignments.text:
Then Catherine suddenly sat upright in her chair,
and clasped her hands together with almost wild
emphasis. "I would marry," she cried, "if I were
you! I would wipe out every recollection. Did they
tell you the pitiful story of a meeting in the train, a
marriage suddenly made up—and who it was that
went away into the darkness in what was to have
been your place?"
assignments.summary: Catherine suddenly becomes animated and gestures toward a mysterious tragic event involving a marriage and a train, urging Hester to marry to overcome some dark recollection.
assignments.best_quote: I would marry if I were you! I would wipe out every recollection. Did they tell you the pitiful story of a meeting in the train, a marriage suddenly made up—and who it was that went away into the darkness in what was to have been your place?

template.name: The Art of Restraint: Oliphant's Achievement

assignments.text:
Edward Vernon, however, was not so fortunate in
his family as in his affairs. He had two sons, one of
whom died young, leaving a little daughter to be [Pg 3] 
brought up by her grandfather; the other "went
wrong." Oh, never-ending family tragedy, never
ending, still beginning, the darkest anguish that
exists in the world!
assignments.summary: Edward Vernon suffered family misfortunes: one son died young leaving a daughter, while his other son 'went wrong,' bringing family shame and suffering.
assignments.best_quote: Oh, never-ending family tragedy, never ending, still beginning, the darkest anguish that exists in the world!

assignments.text:
"That is no answer. One may hate many things
one has to do habitually. Your walk says that you
dislike it. It says, Here am I, who ought to be
guarded like a princess; but I am poor, I have no
escort of honour; yet here I walk, a whole retinue,
a body-guard to myself."
assignments.summary: Edward interprets Hester's gait as a walking contradiction—asserting independence while unconsciously proclaiming her poverty and need for protection—exposing the contradictions she refuses to acknowledge.
assignments.best_quote: Your walk says that you dislike it. It says, Here am I, who ought to be guarded like a princess; but I am poor, I have no escort of honour; yet here I walk, a whole retinue, a body-guard to myself

assignments.text:
"Oh, yes, it is something about you," he said
with a laugh. Then after a pause, "But you have
some insight all the same. No. I'll tell you what
it is; it is money, money, Hester—that is what we
all want. If you had it you would no more marry
Harry than old Rule; if I had it——And the thing
clear is that I must have it," said Edward, breaking
off abruptly. "I can't wait."
assignments.summary: Edward confesses that money is the root of all his complaints—his jealousy, his resentment, his conduct—and that his desperation cannot tolerate delay.
assignments.best_quote: it is money, money, Hester—that is what we all want. If you had it you would no more marry Harry than old Rule; if I had it——And the thing clear is that I must have it. I can't wait

assignments.text:
But when that vagrant sentiment comes in which is
called love (the fools! as if the appropriation of the
name to one kind of affection, and that the most
selfish of all, was not a scorn to love, the real, the
all-enduring!) what was previous virtue, what was
truth, and gratitude, and everything else in life, in
comparison? Of course they must all give place to
the fascination of a pair of shining eyes.
assignments.summary: Oliphant critiques romantic love as a selfish impulse that overrides virtue, truth, gratitude, and family bonds, mocking its supremacy.
assignments.best_quote: when that vagrant sentiment comes in which is called love (the fools! as if the appropriation of the name to one kind of affection, and that the most selfish of all, was not a scorn to love, the real, the all-enduring!)
